R.name: Maker
R.title: works things out with their hands
R.guess: get your hands on something real and make it work
R.desc: You seem to think best with something physical in front of you: tools, materials, a body in motion.
R.why: Practical, physical work with a result you can see.
R.drain: A week of physical, hands-on work
R.card: Whether hands-on, physical work pulls you in. This is the Realistic strand of the Holland model.

I.name: Investigator
I.title: follows questions to the bottom
I.guess: chase a question until it gives up its answer
I.desc: You seem drawn to things that need figuring out, and you stay with a problem after other people move on.
I.why: Runs on curiosity, evidence and figuring things out.
I.drain: A week alone with one hard problem
I.card: Whether puzzles and unexplained things pull you in. This is the Investigative strand.

A.name: Creator
A.title: makes things that were not there before
A.guess: make something that did not exist this morning
A.desc: You seem to want room to shape things your own way, and you notice how things look, sound and feel.
A.why: Open-ended work where your own taste shapes the result.
A.drain: A week with no brief and a blank page
A.card: Whether open-ended making and self-expression pull you in. This is the Artistic strand.

S.name: Helper
S.title: pays attention to people
S.guess: be useful to an actual person in front of you
S.desc: You seem to notice how people are doing, and helping or teaching gives you energy back.
S.why: Centred on helping, teaching or caring for people.
S.drain: A week of looking after other people
S.card: Whether helping, teaching and looking after people pull you in. This is the Social strand.

E.name: Persuader
E.title: gets things moving
E.guess: take charge and get something off the ground
E.desc: You seem comfortable taking the lead, making the case and betting on an idea.
E.why: Rewards initiative, persuasion and taking the lead.
E.drain: A week of pitching and persuading
E.card: Whether leading, selling and taking risks pull you in. This is the Enterprising strand.

C.name: Organizer
C.title: puts things in order
C.desc: You seem to enjoy getting details right and turning a mess into a system that works.
C.why: Rewards accuracy, structure and systems people can rely on.
C.drain: A week of forms, records and checking details
C.card: Whether order, detail and clear systems pull you in. This is the Conventional strand.

d.1: you would rather take the unmarked street than the recommended one
d.-1: you go deep on what you already love instead of chasing what is new

e.1: you come alive around other people
e.-1: you recharge alone and choose your company carefully

f.1: you like things to land, finished and whole
f.-1: the doing is the reward for you, and the finish line is a bonus

t.1: you feel at home in dim light, fog and open questions
t.-1: you lean toward warmth, daylight and things that leave you lighter

styleQuestions.prompt: How often do you re-read or re-watch your favorites?
styleQuestions.measures: Whether depth or breadth feeds you. Returning to favorites is a way of going deeper.

options.t: Constantly. That is what favorites are for.
Rarely. There is too much I have not seen.

styleQuestions.prompt: A year, all expenses paid. One condition:

options.t: Live somewhere I have never been

styleQuestions.prompt: Good news arrives. Your first move:
styleQuestions.measures: Where you process things: out loud with others, or inside first.

options.t: Sit with it alone for a while

styleQuestions.measures: Social energy: groups, pairs, or the conversation you have with yourself.

options.t: In a group, ideas bouncing around

styleQuestions.prompt: After a long trip you can keep only one.
styleQuestions.measures: Process versus outcome: the edited result or the raw experience.

styleQuestions.prompt: A thousand-piece puzzle. The best moment is…
styleQuestions.measures: Whether the reward is in the doing or in the finishing.

options.t: The long middle, sorting and trying

styleQuestions.measures: Mood. People who pick a single lamp in a dark room tend to like mystery and depth.

options.t: One lamp in a dark room

styleQuestions.prompt: Music for a long night drive:
styleQuestions.measures: Mood again, from the angle of sound.

hobbies.name: Budget spreadsheets

hobbies.name: Model railways

hobbies.name: Meal prepping

hobbies.name: Transit and timetable study
hobbies.firstStep: Plan the fastest route through every line in your city.

hobbies.name: Completionist travel
hobbies.firstStep: Visit every station or district in one area.

hobbies.name: Volunteer proofreading
hobbies.firstStep: Proofread a few pages for a public-domain book project.

hobbies.name: Sports statistics
hobbies.firstStep: Build one stats table for your team.

hobbies.name: Club treasurer

hobbies.name: Origami

hobbies.name: Travel points planning

niches.name: Book and paper conservation
niches.what: Repairing rare books, maps and documents so they survive another century.
niches.firstStep: Take a weekend bookbinding class and learn to sew a signature.

niches.name: Field recording for sound libraries
niches.what: Capturing real-world sound that films and games license.
niches.firstStep: Record ten minutes of one place and listen back with headphones.

niches.name: Game narrative design
niches.what: Writing branching stories, dialogue and lore that players move through.
niches.firstStep: Build a tiny branching story in Twine in one evening.

niches.name: Escape room and puzzle design
niches.what: Designing physical and logical puzzles a group solves against a clock.
niches.firstStep: Design one three-step puzzle for friends at your next dinner.

niches.name: Typeface revival
niches.what: Redrawing and digitizing historical typefaces from old printed specimens.
niches.firstStep: Trace five letters from an old book and try them in a free font editor.

niches.name: Data journalism
niches.what: Finding stories hidden in public datasets and turning them into charts and articles.
niches.firstStep: Pick one open dataset about your city and answer a single question with it.

niches.name: Speculative design
niches.what: Making objects and scenarios from possible futures to provoke debate about the present.
niches.firstStep: Sketch an everyday object as it might look in 2060, and write its label.

niches.name: Independent perfumery
niches.what: Composing scents from raw materials, often in small batches.
niches.firstStep: Buy a beginner's kit of single-note materials and learn five by smell.

niches.name: Watch and clock restoration
niches.what: Servicing and restoring mechanical movements.
niches.firstStep: Take apart a cheap mechanical movement and put it back together.

niches.name: Archival research for film and podcasts
niches.what: Digging through archives to find the footage, letters and facts behind a story.
niches.firstStep: Visit a local archive and ask what they hold that nobody requests.

niches.name: Foraging and wild fermentation
niches.what: Finding edible plants and turning them into ferments, vinegars and sodas.
niches.firstStep: Join one guided foraging walk and make one small ferment.

niches.name: Urban exploration photography
niches.what: Documenting forgotten buildings, infrastructure and in-between places.
niches.firstStep: Photograph one overlooked structure in your area at blue hour.

niches.name: Makerspace and community workshop organizing
niches.what: Running shared workshops where people learn to make and repair.
niches.firstStep: Volunteer for one repair café session.

niches.name: Food styling
niches.what: Preparing and arranging food so it photographs the way it tastes.
niches.firstStep: Style and shoot one dish in window light, five different ways.

niches.name: Map and cartographic design
niches.what: Designing maps that are both accurate and beautiful.
niches.firstStep: Hand-draw a map of your neighbourhood with only the places you care about.

niches.name: Tea or coffee sensory evaluation
niches.what: Professional tasting and grading of tea or specialty coffee.
niches.firstStep: Cup three single-origin coffees side by side and take notes.

niches.name: Rare book and ephemera dealing
niches.what: Finding, researching and selling old books, posters, letters and printed oddities.
niches.firstStep: Spend an afternoon in secondhand shops looking for one thing worth researching.

niches.name: Natural dyeing and textile craft
niches.what: Colouring fabric with plants, roots and minerals.
niches.firstStep: Dye one cotton scarf with onion skins.

niches.name: Tabletop RPG design and game mastering
niches.what: Writing adventures and running them for a table of players.
niches.firstStep: Run a one-shot adventure for three friends.

niches.name: Science explainer videos
niches.what: Turning hard ideas into short visual explanations.
niches.firstStep: Explain one concept you love in a 90-second video.

niches.name: Small-garden and native-plant design
niches.what: Designing small outdoor spaces around local plants and wildlife.
niches.firstStep: Plant one container with species native to your area.

niches.name: Oral history collecting
niches.what: Recording and preserving people's spoken memories.
niches.firstStep: Record a 30-minute conversation with an older relative about one year of their life.

niches.name: Lighting design for theatre and spaces
niches.what: Shaping how a room or a stage feels with light alone.
niches.firstStep: Relight one room at home using only lamps you already own.

niches.name: Alternate reality game design
niches.what: Hiding a story across websites, objects and real places for players to uncover.
niches.firstStep: Hide a three-clue trail for a friend across a website, a note and a place.

niches.name: Curating a niche newsletter
niches.what: Finding the best of one small corner of the world and sending it to people who care.
niches.firstStep: Send one issue about your obscure interest to five friends.

niches.name: Natural wine and sommelier work
niches.what: Tasting, sourcing and recommending wines, often from small producers.
niches.firstStep: Taste three natural wines side by side and describe each in one line.

niches.name: Dark-sky tourism guiding
niches.what: Leading night-sky walks and astronomy tours in low-light areas.
niches.firstStep: Find your nearest dark-sky site and go on a moonless night.
